title: Audi AG selects Norfolk Southern-served site for $4 billion Georgia investment
body_markdown:
Audi has announced plans to build its first U.S. manufacturing facility at a[Norfolk Southern-served site](https://nsites.norfolksouthern.com/?sorting=featured_gl=1*1tv1ial*_gcl_aw*R0NMLjE3OTAyNTM0MzcuQ2owS0NRandsTlBWQmhDTUFSSXNBUFo1UnFoT19lRnFoNEp2eFZVUUx3c2tiM1JLUVdTdjhqMGwtV2gwMURQMXJ4WUdSVGM5RTBXaU9HMGFBa2lHRUFMd193Y0I.*_gcl_au*MTExOTg0NDE3MS4xNzg5NDE3NTY5&showpropertyonmap=true&activebasemap2d=Imagery%20Hybrid%20(Places)&mapextent=-9331288.4132008,3839886.801654069,-9334450.995246183,3836475.7992667533&mapzoom=15&propertysearch=georgia&PropertyId=3563455304) in Peach County, Georgia, bringing approximately $4 billion in investments to the region. The project at the Middle Georgia Megasite is expected to create about 4,500 new jobs.


**Top Takeaway**


- The project highlights how rail-served sites can help attract major investment, support efficient supply chains, and create opportunities for communities across Norfolk Southern’s network.


**Connecting investment with opportunity**


The Middle Georgia Megasite offers access to Norfolk Southern’s rail network and rail connections to the ports of Savannah and Brunswick, positioning the location to serve domestic and international markets.


Norfolk Southern was among many partners supporting the project; the Georgia Department of Economic Development; the Mid-Georgia Gateway JDA, which includes Houston, Macon-Bibb, and Peach counties; the Technical College System of Georgia; Georgia Quick Start; University System of Georgia; Georgia Department of Transportation; Georgia Ports Authority; Georgia Environmental Protection Division of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources; Georgia’s Germany-based Europe Office; and Georgia Power.


Audi plans to produce premium SUVs at the facility, with grading beginning in 2027 and construction on the new facility in 2028. Full production is expected in 2031 with an annual capacity of 200,000 vehicles.


**What they’re saying**


“We are proud that Audi has selected Georgia as the home of their first U.S. manufacturing facility, delivering truly historic investment and jobs to middle Georgia. Following the success we've enjoyed with other megasites, we purchased and made more improvements to the Middle Georgia Megasite for just this purpose: to bring a job-creating, high-caliber automotive manufacturer to this region. I want to thank the countless professionals from Peach, Macon-Bibb, and Houston counties in the Mid-Georgia Gateway JDA who helped make this happen. We are excited for hardworking Georgians in Peach County and the entire middle Georgia region to benefit from this project for decades to come. On behalf of the State of Georgia, we are honored to welcome Audi to our state!”
**––**[Governor Brian Kemp](https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-10-24/gov-kemp-audi-ag-selects-georgia-invest-4-billion-first-us-manufacturing)


“We have much greater ambitions for Audi in America, and Georgia will play a central role in making them a reality. With its strong business environment, skilled workforce, and shared ambition, the state is an ideal partner for Audi. We are proud to bring our engineering excellence and pioneering spirit to Georgia. Together, we want to create something that goes far beyond a manufacturing plant: a new home for Audi in America, opportunities for thousands of people and a strong foundation for long-term growth. This investment will bring us closer to our customers and strengthen Audi's competitiveness around the world.”


**–– CEO Gernot Döllner**


“Georgia combines an investment-ready site, skilled workforce, established automotive supplier network and strong logistics infrastructure,”[the company said in its announcement](https://www.audi.com/en/press-releases/audi-to-establish-first-us-production-site-in-georgia-investing-4-billion-and-creating-4500-jobs-18420) . “The Middle Georgia Mega Site also provides the flexibility and space for future expansion.”


**–– Audi**


**What we’re saying**


“Audi’s investment demonstrates how rail-served sites can help attract advanced manufacturing and create lasting economic opportunity. For a manufacturer, a location decision is also a supply chain decision, and rail provides the reach and capacity to connect production with suppliers and customers. Norfolk Southern is proud to work alongside our state and local partners to support this project and help build a foundation for long-term growth in Middle Georgia.”


— **Ed Elkins, Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer, Norfolk Southern**


**The big picture**


Connecting a new manufacturing facility to rail begins well before the first shipment moves. Norfolk Southern’s industrial development team helps businesses identify locations and plan rail infrastructure around their supply chain needs, supporting projects across its 22-state network. Audi’s selection of the Middle Georgia Megasite demonstrates the opportunity that work can help create.


Explore Norfolk Southern’s portfolio of rail-served industrial development sites through[NSites](https://nsites.norfolksouthern.com/) .
